First, I remember that WebSurfer was supposed to look up information about his burial place. They started by searching on DuckDuckGo and found a Find a Grave page for Waylon Jennings. That page mentioned he was buried in the City of Mesa Cemetery in Mesa, Arizona. That seems straightforward, but then WebSurfer tried to load the specific memorial page and kept getting timeouts. That's a problem because if the page doesn't load, you can't get the exact details.

Then, WebSurfer tried again to load the Find a Grave page directly, and this time it worked. They saw that the burial location was indeed City of Mesa Cemetery in Mesa, Arizona. So, that's consistent. But earlier, when they tried to load the Wikipedia page, it didn't show the burial info, which might have caused confusion.

Wait, but then WebSurfer went to Wikipedia and found that Waylon was buried in Chandler, Arizona, at Valley of the Sun Mortuary & Cemetery. That's conflicting because Find a Grave says Mesa. So, there's a discrepancy here. The agent didn't resolve this conflict properly. They just noted both sources but didn't figure out which one is correct.

I think the mistake here is that WebSurfer didn't cross-verify the information from both sources. They found conflicting info, but didn't take the next step to check which one is accurate. Maybe they should have looked up the City of Mesa Cemetery records or checked news articles from the time of his death to see where he was actually buried.

So, the error is that WebSurfer didn't properly resolve the conflict between the two sources. They identified the conflict but didn't take the necessary steps to confirm which source was accurate. This led to an unclear answer, making it hard to know for sure where he's buried.

In terms of the step where the mistake occurred, WebSurfer first encountered the conflict when they found both Mesa and Chandler mentioned. That must have been step 6 or so. From then on, they didn't fully resolve it, so the error started there.
